subject: Audit sandbox: retention window & exception proposal
messages:
From: Nora Liu <nora.liu@nomahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: audit@nomahealth.com
Date: 2027-06-12T09:15:00Z
Subject: Audit snapshot & retention mapping for sandbox logs

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

We are starting collection for Noma Health's upcoming vendor assessment (requested by our auditors). Two asks:

1) For sandbox/preview environments, can you provide a matrix that maps each audit log type (authn events, API request logs, model inference traces, KV/cache keys references) to your default retention and whether PII is redacted or stored? We need this to show auditors what data flows look like across environments.

2) We also expect a small carve-out: our compliance team wants a short-term exception to retain a subset of sandbox logs longer (up to 12 months) for a narrow set of customers during parallel validation. What process do we need to follow to request that exemption and what controls would you require (e.g., BYOK scoping, key rotation cadence)?

Attachments: requested_snapshot_spec.pdf (simple spec of fields we will ask you to include in the snapshot).

Can you confirm a timeline? Auditor kickoff is 2027-06-24.

Thanks,
Nora Liu
Security Operations 
Noma Health

--
Nora Liu
Noma Health | Security Ops
N: +1 415 555 0191

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Nora Liu <nora.liu@nomahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot & retention mapping for sandbox logs

Thanks Nora — we can support this, and I want to make sure we scope the request so it's operationally safe. Quick triage below and next steps.

Summary of what we'll deliver by 2027-06-18: a retention matrix (CSV/XLSX) that lists log class, default retention, PII handling, access controls, and whether the artifact is included in a snapshot export for audits. We'll also include an exception intake template that captures justification, exact scopes, and approval fields.

Operational constraints / questions:
- For "model inference traces" — do you need full token-level traces, or a summarized provenance record? Full traces are large and include prompt content; summarization/redaction reduces risk.
- BYOK scoping: do you want an escrow-style key for only the retained sandbox snapshots, or to use your org-level KMS for all customer-specific sandbox exports?
- Exemption governance: we typically require an approved runbook, dedicated access roles, and a retention cutoff that auto-deletes. Will Noma accept time-limited access and an attested reviewer?

Karthik / Marissa / Evelyn — can you take the lead on building the matrix + a short proposal for exemption controls? I suggest we draft 3 options (baseline 90d, limited-exempt 365d with BYOK scoping, and a controlled-archive path for legal/audit only). I will own coordination with Noma and the auditor.

Jonas
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Nora Liu <nora.liu@nomahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-13T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot & retention mapping for sandbox logs

Adding product/infra perspective and proposed defaults. See attached retention_matrix_v1.xlsx and snapshot-ops-runbook.md (runbook stub).

Proposed defaults (rationale included in worksheet):
- AuthN / authZ events: default 365d (low volume, necessary for investigations)
- API request logs (headers, method, timestamp, truncated URIs): default 90d; PII in payloads must be redacted by default
- Model inference traces: default 30d summarized telemetry; full traces only via explicit exception request and stored under customer-scoped BYOK bucket
- KV/cache audit indicators (miss/hit counters, key ids): default 14d; key contents never stored in cleartext in snapshots

Exemption pathway (proposal):
1) Intake form (we'll draft) that defines customer, scope, exact fields, duration, and business justification.
2) Approval: Security + Product + Legal sign-off for any >90d retention.
3) Controls: BYOK scoping to a customer-specific KMS key OR encrypted archive with HSM-wrapped keys; access logged; auto-expiration enforced by lifecycle policy.

Operational notes:
- For short-term 12-month exceptions we can create a segregated bucket with a separate lifecycle policy; however we need Noma to provide a KMS key or accept Redwood-managed envelope keys with attestation.
- We'll need an on-call window to run the snapshot and a runbook for safe extraction (attached).

Next steps I own: update the matrix with column for "estimated monthly size" and a draft exemption intake template. Target: 2027-06-15 EOD.

Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Infra
Redwood Inference

Attachments: retention_matrix_v1.xlsx, snapshot-ops-runbook.md

From: Nora Liu <nora.liu@nomahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T14:32:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit snapshot & retention mapping for sandbox logs

Jonas / Karthik — this is excellent, thanks for the fast turnaround. A few quick clarifications:

- For our audit scope we only need summarized inference provenance (timestamps, model id, call metadata, and anonymized outputs). We will not request token-level content.
- Noma prefers to provide a BYOK key for any 12-month exception; procurement will open the KMS onboarding ticket if you send the required parameters.
- Accept the proposed intake/approval flow. Please include a checkbox in the intake for "attested reviewer" and a required expiry date.

We can do a 30-minute kickoff on 2027-06-18 at 10:00 PT to confirm the final matrix and schedule the snapshot run. I will share a Drive folder with auditors and the DocuSign link for the KMS onboarding form after procurement confirms.

Thanks,
Nora

Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
